ARCOUNT.summary: Counts the elements that are set in an array.

ARDEL.summary: Clears the elements at the given array positions.
ARDEL.complexity: O(N), N being how many positions are given.

ARDELRANGE.summary: Clears every element inside one or more position ranges of an array.
ARDELRANGE.complexity: Grows with the elements and slices that exist inside the ranges, not with how wide the ranges are.

ARGET.summary: Reads the element stored at one array position.

ARGETRANGE.summary: Reads the elements between two array positions.
ARGETRANGE.complexity: O(N), N being the width of the range.

ARGREP.summary: Finds the array positions in a range whose elements match exact, glob, regular expression or substring predicates.
ARGREP.complexity: O(P*C), P being the positions visited in the slices touched and C the cost of testing one element.

ARINFO.summary: Describes how an array is stored, optionally slice by slice.
ARINFO.complexity: O(1), or O(N) with FULL, N being the number of slices.

ARINSERT.summary: Writes values at the array's insertion cursor and advances it.
ARINSERT.complexity: O(N), N being how many values are written.

ARLASTITEMS.summary: Reads the most recently inserted elements of an array.
ARLASTITEMS.complexity: O(N), N being the count asked for.

ARLEN.summary: Returns one past the highest array position that holds an element.

ARMGET.summary: Reads the elements at several array positions.
ARMGET.complexity: O(N), N being how many positions are given.

ARMSET.summary: Writes several position and value pairs into an array.
ARMSET.complexity: O(N), N being how many pairs are given.

ARNEXT.summary: Returns the position the next ARINSERT will write to.

AROP.summary: Folds the elements in an array range into one result such as a sum, minimum, maximum, bitwise value, match count or used count.
AROP.complexity: O(P), P being the positions visited in the slices touched. At worst that is the width of the range; usually it is close to the elements present.

ARRING.summary: Writes values into an array used as a fixed-size ring, overwriting the oldest ones.
ARRING.complexity: O(M) for M values, plus O(N) when the ring is resized, N being the larger of the old and new sizes.

ARSCAN.summary: Walks the elements present in an array range, returning positions with their values.
ARSCAN.complexity: O(P), P being the positions visited in the slices touched. At worst that is the width of the range; usually it is close to the elements present.

ARSEEK.summary: Moves the array's insertion cursor to a position.

ARSET.summary: Writes one or more consecutive values starting at an array position.
ARSET.complexity: O(N), N being how many values are written.

BACKUP.summary: Takes and manages online backups of the dataset. Use a subcommand.

BACKUP ABORT.summary: Stops the backup that is running.

BACKUP CLEANUP.summary: Removes the files left by finished or aborted backups.

BACKUP SEAL.summary: Finishes a backup so it can be restored from.

BACKUP STATUS.summary: Reports the progress of the current backup.

BLMOVEM.summary: Moves several elements from one list to another, waiting until the source has them.
BLMOVEM.complexity: O(N), N being how many elements move.

CLUSTER MIGRATION.summary: Starts, cancels or reports on moving slot ranges into this node.
CLUSTER MIGRATION.complexity: O(N), N being the number of slots in the ranges given.

DELEX.summary: Deletes a key, optionally only when its value or value digest matches a condition.
DELEX.complexity: O(1) for IFEQ and IFNE. O(N) for IFDEQ and IFDNE, N being the length of the value.

DIGEST.summary: Returns a hash digest of a string value.
DIGEST.complexity: O(N), N being the length of the value.

FT.AGGREGATE.summary: Runs a query against an index and passes the matches through grouping, reducing, sorting, applying and filtering steps.
FT.AGGREGATE.complexity: O(N), N being the documents the query and pipeline process.

FT.ALIASADD.summary: Gives an index an additional name.

FT.ALIASLIST.summary: Lists the aliases that point at an index.
FT.ALIASLIST.complexity: O(N), N being the number of aliases.

FT.ALIASUPDATE.summary: Points an alias at a different index, creating the alias if needed.

FT.ALTER.summary: Adds a field to the schema of an existing index.
FT.ALTER.complexity: O(N), N being the keys reindexed.

FT.CREATE.summary: Defines a new index over hash or JSON keys with a given schema.
FT.CREATE.complexity: O(K) for K schema fields, plus O(N) over the keyspace when existing keys are indexed.

FT.CURSOR READ.summary: Fetches the next batch of rows from an aggregation cursor.

FT.DEBUG COMPACT.summary: Compacts the vector graph of one vector field.
FT.DEBUG COMPACT.complexity: O(N), N being the vectors in the field.

FT.DICTADD.summary: Adds terms to a custom dictionary.

FT.DICTDEL.summary: Removes terms from a custom dictionary.

FT.DICTDUMP.summary: Lists the terms in a custom dictionary.
FT.DICTDUMP.complexity: O(N), N being the terms in the dictionary.

FT.DROPINDEX.summary: Removes an index, and with DD also the documents it covers.
FT.DROPINDEX.complexity: O(1), or O(N) with DD, N being the keys deleted.

FT.EXPLAIN.summary: Shows how a query is parsed into an execution plan.

FT.EXPLAINCLI.summary: Shows a query's execution plan as an array of lines, handy in redis-cli.

FT.HYBRID.summary: Combines a text query and a vector similarity query over one index and fuses their scores.
FT.HYBRID.complexity: O(N+M), N being the cost of the text query and M the cost of the vector query.

FT.INFO.summary: Reports the definition and statistics of an index.

FT.PROFILE.summary: Runs a search, aggregate or hybrid query and reports where the time went.
FT.PROFILE.complexity: O(N), the cost of the profiled query.

FT.SEARCH.summary: Queries an index and returns matching documents or their keys.
FT.SEARCH.complexity: O(N), N being the documents the query visits.

FT.SPELLCHECK.summary: Suggests corrections for misspelled query terms.

FT.SYNDUMP.summary: Lists the synonym groups of an index.

FT.SYNUPDATE.summary: Creates or extends a synonym group of an index.

FT.TAGVALS.summary: Lists the distinct values stored in a tag field.
FT.TAGVALS.complexity: O(N), N being the distinct values.

FT._LIST.summary: Lists the names of all indexes.

HIMPORT.summary: Bulk loads hashes through a field set prepared once per connection. Use a subcommand.

HIMPORT DISCARD.summary: Forgets one field set prepared on this connection.
HIMPORT DISCARD.complexity: O(N), N being the field sets held by the connection.

HIMPORT DISCARDALL.summary: Forgets every field set prepared on this connection.
HIMPORT DISCARDALL.complexity: O(N), N being the field sets held by the connection.

HIMPORT PREPARE.summary: Names a list of hash fields on this connection for later HIMPORT SET calls.
HIMPORT PREPARE.complexity: O(N*log(N)), N being the number of fields.

HIMPORT SET.summary: Writes a hash using a prepared field set, taking only the values.
HIMPORT SET.complexity: O(N), N being the fields in the set.

HOTKEYS.summary: Samples and reports the most used keys. Use a subcommand.

HOTKEYS GET.summary: Returns the hottest keys found so far.
HOTKEYS GET.complexity: O(K), K being how many keys are returned.

HOTKEYS RESET.summary: Clears the collected hot key data.

HOTKEYS START.summary: Begins tracking hot keys by CPU or network use.

HOTKEYS STOP.summary: Ends hot key tracking and keeps the results.

INCREX.summary: Adds to a numeric value with optional bounds, saturation and expiry, all in one step.

JSON.ARRAPPEND.summary: Adds values to the end of the arrays found at a path.
JSON.ARRAPPEND.complexity: O(1) per array matched; O(N) in the size of the document when the path matches many values.

JSON.ARRINDEX.summary: Finds where a value first appears in the arrays at a path.
JSON.ARRINDEX.complexity: O(N), N being the array length, or the document size when the path matches many values.

JSON.ARRINSERT.summary: Inserts values before a position in the arrays at a path.
JSON.ARRINSERT.complexity: O(N), N being the array length, or the document size when the path matches many values.

JSON.ARRLEN.summary: Returns the length of the arrays at a path.
JSON.ARRLEN.complexity: O(1) per array matched; O(N) in the size of the document when the path matches many values.

JSON.ARRPOP.summary: Removes and returns an element from the arrays at a path, by default the last.
JSON.ARRPOP.complexity: O(1) when popping the last element, otherwise O(N) in the array length; O(N) in the document size when the path matches many values.

JSON.ARRTRIM.summary: Cuts the arrays at a path down to a position range.
JSON.ARRTRIM.complexity: O(N), N being the array length, or the document size when the path matches many values.

JSON.CLEAR.summary: Empties arrays and objects and zeroes numbers at a path.
JSON.CLEAR.complexity: O(N), N being the size of the values cleared.

JSON.DEBUG MEMORY.summary: Reports how many bytes a JSON value takes.
JSON.DEBUG MEMORY.complexity: O(N), N being the size of the value.

JSON.DEL.summary: Removes the values at a path, or the whole document.
JSON.DEL.complexity: O(N), N being the size of what is removed.

JSON.FORGET.complexity: O(N), N being the size of what is removed.

JSON.GET.summary: Returns the values at one or more paths, serialised as JSON.
JSON.GET.complexity: O(N), N being the size of what is returned.

JSON.MERGE.summary: Merges a JSON value into the document at a path, following JSON Merge Patch rules.
JSON.MERGE.complexity: O(M+N), M being the size of the existing value and N the size of the patch.

JSON.MGET.summary: Returns the value at one path from several documents.
JSON.MGET.complexity: O(N), N being the total size of what is returned.

JSON.MSET.summary: Sets values at paths in several documents in one atomic step.
JSON.MSET.complexity: O(K*(M+N)) for K triplets, M being the size of each existing value and N of each new one.

JSON.NUMINCRBY.summary: Adds a number to the numeric values at a path.

JSON.NUMMULTBY.summary: Multiplies the numeric values at a path by a number.

JSON.OBJKEYS.summary: Lists the member names of the objects at a path.
JSON.OBJKEYS.complexity: O(N), N being the members returned.

JSON.OBJLEN.summary: Counts the members of the objects at a path.

JSON.RESP.summary: Returns the value at a path translated into RESP types.
JSON.RESP.complexity: O(N), N being the size of the value.

JSON.SET.summary: Stores a JSON value at a path, creating the document if needed.
JSON.SET.complexity: O(M+N), M being the size of the value replaced and N the size of the new one.

JSON.STRAPPEND.summary: Appends text to the strings at a path.

JSON.STRLEN.summary: Returns the length of the strings at a path.

JSON.TOGGLE.summary: Flips the booleans at a path.

JSON.TYPE.summary: Names the JSON type of the values at a path.

LMOVEM.summary: Moves several elements from one list to another in one step.
LMOVEM.complexity: O(N), N being how many elements move.

SDIFFCARD.summary: Counts the members of the first set that are in none of the others, without building the result.
SDIFFCARD.complexity: O(N), N being the members across all the sets.

SUNIONCARD.summary: Counts the distinct members across several sets, exactly or approximately, without building the result.
SUNIONCARD.complexity: O(N), N being the members across all the sets.

TS.ADD.summary: Appends a sample to a time series, creating the series if needed.
TS.ADD.complexity: O(1), plus O(M) when M compaction rules are attached.

TS.ALTER.summary: Changes the retention, chunk size, duplicate policy or labels of a time series.
TS.ALTER.complexity: O(N), N being the labels changed.

TS.CREATERULE.summary: Attaches a compaction rule that rolls samples from one series into buckets in another.

TS.DECRBY.summary: Subtracts from the latest sample of a time series, or starts one.
TS.DECRBY.complexity: O(1), plus O(M) when M compaction rules are attached.

TS.DEL.summary: Removes the samples between two timestamps.
TS.DEL.complexity: O(N), N being the samples removed.

TS.GET.summary: Returns the newest sample of a time series.

TS.INCRBY.summary: Adds to the latest sample of a time series, or starts one.
TS.INCRBY.complexity: O(1), plus O(M) when M compaction rules are attached.

TS.INFO.summary: Reports the settings, labels, rules and size of a time series.

TS.MADD.summary: Appends samples to several time series at once.
TS.MADD.complexity: O(N), N being the samples, times the compaction rules on each series.

TS.MGET.summary: Returns the newest sample of every time series whose labels match a filter.
TS.MGET.complexity: O(N), N being the series that match.

TS.MRANGE.summary: Reads a time range, oldest first, from every series whose labels match a filter.
TS.MRANGE.complexity: O(N/C+K), N being the samples in the series, C the samples per chunk and K the samples returned.

TS.MREVRANGE.summary: Reads a time range, newest first, from every series whose labels match a filter.
TS.MREVRANGE.complexity: O(N/C+K), N being the samples in the series, C the samples per chunk and K the samples returned.

TS.NRANGE.summary: Reads a time range, oldest first, from a list of named time series.
TS.NRANGE.complexity: O(numkeys*(N/C+K)), N being the samples per series, C the samples per chunk and K the samples returned.

TS.NREVRANGE.summary: Reads a time range, newest first, from a list of named time series.
TS.NREVRANGE.complexity: O(numkeys*(N/C+K)), N being the samples per series, C the samples per chunk and K the samples returned.

TS.QUERYINDEX.summary: Lists the keys of the time series whose labels match a filter.
TS.QUERYINDEX.complexity: O(N), N being the series that match.

TS.QUERYLABELS.summary: Lists label names, or the values of one label, across the time series matching a filter.
TS.QUERYLABELS.complexity: O(N), N being the series that match.

TS.RANGE.summary: Reads the samples of a time series in a time range, oldest first.
TS.RANGE.complexity: O(N/C+K), N being the samples in the series, C the samples per chunk and K the samples returned.

TS.READ.summary: Reads samples newer than a timestamp, optionally waiting for them to arrive.
TS.READ.complexity: O(log(N)+K), N being the samples in the series and K the samples returned.

TS.REVRANGE.summary: Reads the samples of a time series in a time range, newest first.
TS.REVRANGE.complexity: O(N/C+K), N being the samples in the series, C the samples per chunk and K the samples returned.

VADD.summary: Inserts an element with its vector into a vector set, or replaces the vector of an existing one.

VCARD.summary: Counts the elements of a vector set.

VDIM.summary: Returns how many dimensions the vectors in a set have.

VEMB.summary: Returns the stored vector of an element.

VGETATTR.summary: Returns the JSON attributes attached to an element.

VINFO.summary: Reports how a vector set is configured and stored.

VISMEMBER.summary: Tells whether an element is in a vector set.

VLINKS.summary: Lists an element's neighbours in the graph, layer by layer.

VRANDMEMBER.summary: Returns one or more random elements of a vector set.

VRANGE.summary: Lists elements of a vector set in lexicographic order between two bounds.

VREM.summary: Removes an element from a vector set.

VSETATTR.summary: Attaches JSON attributes to an element, or clears them.

VSIM.summary: Finds the elements most similar to a vector or to another element, with an optional attribute filter.

XACKDEL.summary: Acknowledges stream entries for a group and deletes them, with control over references from other groups.

XCFGSET.summary: Sets the idempotent producer settings of a stream.

XDELEX.summary: Deletes stream entries, with control over references held by consumer groups.

XIDMPRECORD.summary: Records a producer and message id pair against a stream entry for idempotent adds.

XNACK.summary: Hands pending stream entries back to a group without acknowledging them.
